children.text: This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document defines the requirements for the volunteer management system (VMS), a new product that can organize volunteers and requests for them so seniors and students looking for support can be helped more efficiently
Project managers should read sections 1 and 2. Developers should refer to section 2, particularly the use cases and user requirements to support development of the product.
Any section which has not been completed in the current iteration of the project will be marked as TBD

This document details the software requirements specification for the Volunteer Management System version 1.0. It is intended to help developers have a clear idea of the system functions and help project managers understand the user requirements.
User classes are classified as Direct or Indirect, and as Favoured, Disfavoured, or Ignored.
Use case IDs use the format UC-#; preconditions, postconditions, and exceptions are labelled PRE-#, POST-#, and E#.
Dates use DD/MM/YYYY.
"TBD" marks information not yet available.
Please refer to the linked vision and scope document

The Volunteer Management System (VMS) is a new product that is intended to organize volunteers and requests for them to more efficiently help seniors who need support. The VMS interfaces with a government system to validate police background checks of volunteers before they are approved for the VMS.

Use Case 3

ID and Name:

UC-3 Create New Volunteer

Author:

Jay Erickson

Date Created:

18/10/2026

Primary Actor:

Volunteer

Secondary Actors:

System Administrator

Description:

Create a new volunteer profile to add to the VMS. This profile is based on personal information the potential volunteer provides and is entered into the system by a system administrator.

Trigger:

A potential volunteer contacts a system administrator wanting to become a volunteer and provides personal information about themself.

Preconditions:

None

Postconditions:

POST-1. A volunteer profile is added to the VMS.

POST-2. The profile awaits approval for police background and required education checks.

Normal Flow:

1.0   Person wants to sign up as a volunteer.

1.1   Person provides personal information to system administrators.

1.2 System Administrator creates a blank volunteer profile

1.3 System Administrator fills in the volunteer profile with information provided by the person.

1.4 Volunteer profile is added to the VMS.

Alternative Flows:

1.1.1 Person provides personal information to the VMS digitally and waits to be approved and officially added to the system later by a system administrator. 

Exceptions:

1.1.E1 Personal information is invalid, illegible, or incomplete.

Priority:

High

Business Rules:

TBD When business rules are understood.

Assumptions:

Potential volunteers can contact system administrators. Volunteers provide accurate personal information to the best of their ability. It is the job of system administrators to create new volunteer profiles.

Other Information:

 None

Use Case 4

ID and Name:

UC-4 Approve New Volunteer

Author:

Bre Mayall

Date Created:

18/10/2026

Primary Actor:

Volunteer Administrator

Secondary Actors:

Background Check System (BCS); Police Officer (for manual approval); certificate verification source (when applicable)

Description:

The Volunteer Administrator reviews a new volunteer’s application and approves it after the required screening, background check, and (when applicable) educational certificate verification are complete.

Trigger:

The Volunteer Administrator selects a new volunteer profile for approval.

Preconditions:

PRE-1. The administrator is authenticated and authorized to approve volunteers.
  PRE-2. The volunteer profile has been submitted, and initial screening is complete.
  PRE-3. The required background-check result, including any required police approval, has been received.
  PRE-4. Educational certificates have been verified if the volunteer will teach young children.

Postconditions:

 POST-1. The volunteer’s status is saved as Approved.
  POST-2. The approval decision is recorded in the VMS.

Normal Flow:

1.     Administrator opens the list of new volunteer registrations.

2.     VMS displays volunteer profiles and their screening/check statuses.

3.     Administrator selects a volunteer whose required checks are complete.

4.     VMS displays the volunteer’s profile and verification results.

5.     Administrator selects Approve.

6.     VMS validates that all required checks are complete and saves the approval.

7.     VMS updates the volunteer status to Approved and confirms the result.

Alternative Flows:

1.    Certificate verification applies (branches from 3): If the volunteer will teach young children, the administrator confirms the educational certificates are verified before approving; then continue at 5

2.    Further review needed (branches from 4): The administrator does not approve the application and leaves it pending for further review.

Exceptions:

E1 — Background check pending or incomplete: VMS prevents approval and displays the outstanding check status

E2 — Required certificate verification missing: VMS prevents approval when the volunteer will teach young children.

E3 — Save/network failure: VMS reports that approval was not confirmed and does not show Approved unless the change was successfully saved.

Priority:

High

Business Rules:

No rule identifiers are provided in the supplied requirements document. Applicable rule: a volunteer must pass the required background check before approval; educational certificates must be verified for volunteers teaching young children.

Assumptions:

The Volunteer Administrator is the final approver. BCS performs background checks, with police approval handled manually during working hours. Certificate verification is required only for volunteers who will teach young children.

Other Information:

Only authorized administrators may approve volunteers. The VMS should retain an auditable approval status. If a system or network failure occurs, the approval must not be treated as complete unless the status change is saved successfully

  POST-2. The approval decision is recorded in the VMS.

Normal Flow:

1.     Administrator opens the list of new volunteer registrations.

2.     VMS displays volunteer profiles and their screening/check statuses.

3.     Administrator selects a volunteer whose required checks are complete.

4.     VMS displays the volunteer’s profile and verification results.

5.     Administrator selects Approve.

6.     VMS validates that all required checks are complete and saves the approval.

7.     VMS updates the volunteer status to Approved and confirms the result.

Alternative Flows:

1.    Certificate verification applies (branches from 3): If the volunteer will teach young children, the administrator confirms the educational certificates are verified before approving; then continue at 5

2.    Further review needed (branches from 4): The administrator does not approve the application and leaves it pending for further review.

Exceptions:

E1 — Background check pending or incomplete: VMS prevents approval and displays the outstanding check status

E2 — Required certificate verification missing: VMS prevents approval when the volunteer will teach young children.

E3 — Save/network failure: VMS reports that approval was not confirmed and does not show Approved unless the change was successfully saved.

Priority:

High

Business Rules:

No rule identifiers are provided in the supplied requirements document. Applicable rule: a volunteer must pass the required background check before approval; educational certificates must be verified for volunteers teaching young children.

Assumptions:

The Volunteer Administrator is the final approver. BCS performs background checks, with police approval handled manually during working hours. Certificate verification is required only for volunteers who will teach young children.

Other Information:

Only authorized administrators may approve volunteers. The VMS should retain an auditable approval status. If a system or network failure occurs, the approval must not be treated as complete unless the status change is saved successfully

Policies of privacy and security of personal information.
Interfacing with a government system to validate background checks.

The VMS is dependent on a government system to validate volunteer background checks. Said government system is currently under development to be fully automated within the next few months. The VMS could be further delayed if the government system is not complete by that time.
The VMS is assumed to have enough volunteers to handle senior cases. If not enough volunteers are available then senior cases will have less support and might cause a backup of unresolved cases.

children.heading: Description
children.text:
Create a new volunteer profile to add to the VMS. This profile is based on personal information the potential volunteer provides and is entered into the system by a system administrator.

High Priority

children.heading: Stimulus/Response Sequences
children.text: A potential volunteer contacts a system administrator wanting to become a volunteer and provides personal information about themself.

children.heading: Functional Requirement 1
children.text: When an administrator wants to create a new volunteer to the VMS, the system shall create a blank volunteer profile template with fillable sections for information including name, date of birth, background check, education, experience, and notes on the person.

children.heading: Functional Requirement 2
children.text: When the administrator is finished filling out the template and wants to save the information, the system shall save the information to the VMS database to be viewed or edited by other administrators with permissions to the VMS.

children.heading: Functional Requirement 3
children.text: When saving a new profile if there exists another profile with identical information the system shall display a warning before saving that this profile already exists and prompt the administrator to edit the original profile instead or send a request to a systems administrator to override this error.

children.heading: Functional Requirement 4
children.text: If the profile is not filled out with necessary information the system shall display a warning to the administrator and highlight what needed information is missing. The system shall be able to save with incomplete information but shall flag the profile as incomplete.

children.heading: Description
children.text:
The Volunteer Administrator reviews a new volunteer’s application and approves it afterthe required screening, background check, and (when applicable) educational certificateverification are complete.Create a new volunteer profile to add to the VMS. This profile is based on personal information the potential volunteer provides and is entered into the system by a system administrator.

High Priority

children.heading: Stimulus/Response Sequences
children.text: The Volunteer Administrator selects a new volunteer profile for approval

children.heading: Functional Requirement 1
children.text: If a volunteer needs approval for a background check an administrator shall send a request to the system and it shall forward the request and the profile to the government system for background checks. The system shall display when the background check request has been sent and is complete and the status of the request if it is approved, in progress, or canceled.

children.heading: Functional Requirements 2
children.text: If all checks for the profile are validated and an administrator approves of it, the administrator can select Approve on the profile and it shall be flagged as an approved profile that can be assigned cases.

children.heading: Description
children.text:
Generate a daily report of the forecasted number of cases for the next week

Low Priority

children.heading: Stimulus/Response Sequences
children.text: Automatic (daily)

children.heading: Functional Requirement 1
children.text: The system shall output daily predictions of the number of cases and volunteer availability for the next week. These predictions shall be based on report case history that is analyzed and put through a prediction algorithm. These daily outputs shall be saved for future access.

children.heading: Functional Requirement 2
children.text: Daily case predictions should be displayed to volunteer administrators in a visual medium that is easy to understand and allows options to show more information on how these predictions are made and what data is used.

Interested case types: list, zero or more. Case type list TBD.

Assignment status: Not assigned or Assigned.
Engagement score: number from 0 to 100. System-calculated; formula TBD.
Date created: DD/MM/YYYY. System-set.

children.heading: DD-2 Senior Case
children.text: A request for support for a senior, reported by a Client Ambassador (UC-1) and matched to a volunteer (UC-5).
Case ID: text, 10 characters. Unique, system-generated.
Senior name / contact: text, up to 100 characters. Required.
Case type: enumeration. Values TBD.
Health issues: text, up to 500 characters. Optional; added via UC-6.
Date reported: DD/MM/YYYY. Cannot be in the future.
Case status: Unassigned, Pending acceptance or Assigned. Closed TBD.

children.heading: DD-3 Assignment
children.text: Links one volunteer to one case (UC-5). A volunteer’s Assignments make up their volunteering history.
Assignment ID: text. Unique, system-generated.
Case ID: reference to an existing case with status Unassigned.
Volunteer ID: reference to an Approved volunteer with status Not assigned.
Assigned by: reference to the Volunteer Administrator.
Date assigned: DD/MM/YYYY. System-set on confirmation.
Volunteer response: Pending, Accepted or Declined. The case becomes Assigned only when the response is Accepted.

children.heading: DD-4 Background Check Record
children.text: Police background check result for one volunteer, required before approval (UC-4).
Check ID: text. Unique, system-generated.
Volunteer ID: reference to an existing volunteer profile.
Check status: Pending, Passed or Failed.
Police approval: yes/no. Manual checks only.
Date submitted / completed: DD/MM/YYYY. Completed cannot be before submitted.

children.heading: DD-5 Daily Forecast Report
children.text: Automatically generated forecast of cases for the next week (UC-7), stored for later access.
Report ID: text. Unique, system-generated.
Date generated: DD/MM/YYYY. One per day.
Forecast period: the 7 days after Date generated.
Forecasted cases per day: 7 whole numbers, each 0 or more.
Total forecasted cases: whole number. Sum of the daily values.
